newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close firm despite elections.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close firm despite elections.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed marginally higher on Friday, with investors ignoring the shortened trading session due to local elections to actively seek selected shares, brokers said.
The all-share index closed 0.65 points higher at 633.30. Price gains outnumbered losses by 13 to seven. James Finlay rose 2.75 rupees to 57.75, Ceylon Glass 50 cents to 22.

"There was no evidence of the lethargy expected due to elections and curtailed trading, with buyers willing to take growth stocks if price and quantity were right," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, a trader at Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
Turnover was 27.5 million rupees supported by blue chips. Parcels of 51,200 Development Finance Corporation, 20,300 John Keells Holdings and one million Distilleries Co were the main trades.
Because of local government elections trading on the Colombo exchange was limited to between 9 a.m. (0300 GMT) and 11.30 a.m instead of the usual 9 a.m to 12.40 p.m.

Sri Lankans are voting to elect members to 238 local councils in what is widely seen as the first political test of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance government. -- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
